    print(diff.head(8))
    print('total diff:', anom['unblended_cost'].sum() - base_med.sum())

import pandas as pd, numpy as np
df = pd.read_csv('data.csv')
acc = df[df.account_id=='xykrZYR'].copy()
acc['dt'] = pd.to_datetime(acc['date'], format='%m/%d/%y')
base = acc[acc.dt < '2025-10-20']

anom = acc[acc.dt == '2025-10-20'].copy()
keys = ['csp','cloud_service','application','instance_family']

# per-key baseline: mean and std of daily cost
g = base.groupby(keys)['unblended_cost'].agg(['mean','std','count'])
anom_sum = anom.groupby(keys)['unblended_cost'].sum().rename('anom')
m = anom_sum.to_frame().join(g)
m['z'] = (m['anom'] - m['mean'])/m['std']
m['diff'] = m['anom'] - m['mean']
print(m.sort_values('diff', ascending=False).head(15).to_string())
print()
# total anomaly excess vs baseline mean per day
print('total anom:', m['anom'].sum(), 'total base mean:', m['mean'].sum(), 'excess:', m['diff'].sum())

import pandas as pd, numpy as np
df = pd.read_csv('data.csv')
acc = df[df.account_id=='xykrZYR'].copy()
acc['dt'] = pd.to_datetime(acc['date'], format='%m/%d/%y')
base = acc[acc.dt < '2025-10-20']

anom = acc[acc.dt == '2025-10-20'].copy()
keys = ['csp','cloud_service','application','instance_family']

# per-key baseline stats on num_instances and price
g = base.groupby(keys).agg(ni_mean=('num_instances','mean'), ni_std=('num_instances','std'),
                           p_mean=('price','mean'), p_min=('price','min'), p_max=('price','max'))
a = anom.groupby(keys).agg(ni=('num_instances','sum'), p=('price','first'))
m = a.join(g)
# flag rows where price deviates from baseline range, or ni is far above baseline
m['ni_dev'] = (m['ni'] - m['ni_mean'])/m['ni_std'].replace(0,np.nan)
price_out = (m['p'] < m['p_min']) | (m['p'] > m['p_max'])
print('price out of baseline range:', price_out.sum())
print(m[price_out].to_string())
big = m[m['ni_dev'] > 2]
print('num_instances z>2:', len(big))
print(big.to_string())
# also check rows with baseline ni_mean==0 but ni>0
zero = m[(m['ni_mean']==0) & (m['ni']>0)]
print('zero->positive:', zero.to_string())

df = pd.read_csv('data.csv')
acc = df[df.account_id=='xykrZYR'].copy()

# excess over median baseline per key, for all keys
base_med = base.groupby(keys)['unblended_cost'].median()

m = anom_sum.to_frame().join(base_med.rename('med'))
m['excess'] = m['anom'] - m['med']
tot = m['excess'].sum()
print('total excess over median:', tot)
top = m.sort_values('excess', ascending=False).head(10)
print(top.to_string())
print('top share:', top['excess'].sum()/tot)
# threshold: excess > 20 (i.e. > ~10% of total)
big = m[m['excess'] > 20]
print(big.to_string())

a = anom.groupby(keys).agg(ni=('num_instances','sum'), p=('price','first'))
m = a.join(g)
# flag rows where price deviates from baseline range, or ni is far above baseline
m['ni_dev'] = (m['ni'] - m['ni_mean'])/m['ni_std'].replace(0,np.nan)
price_out = (m['p'] < m['p_min']) | (m['p'] > m['p_max'])
print('price out of baseline range:', price_out.sum())
print(m[price_out].to_string())
big = m[m['ni_dev'] > 2]
print('num_instances z>2:', len(big))
print(big.to_string())
# also check rows with baseline ni_mean==0 but ni>0
zero = m[(m['ni_mean']==0) & (m['ni']>0)]
print('zero->positive:', zero.to_string())"}
